proposals.expected_failure_mode: H compartment may be weakly identifiable with only 31 training weeks, leading to parameter tradeoffs (e.g., I->H vs H outflow) and unstable forecasts.
proposals.rationale: Matches target semantics (hospitalization rate) via an explicit H compartment; SEIR core can capture sharp, high-peaked seasonal waves while mapping directly to admissions.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Over-attribution between I and H can inflate uncertainty and produce unrealistic decomposition, especially around the peak (identifiability issues).
proposals.rationale: Allows observed hospitalization-rate signal to be represented as a mixture of infectious burden and hospitalization occupancy/admissions proxy, which can improve fit when the surveillance signal blends processes or reporting artifacts.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the hospitalization process has longer/variable delays or distinct dynamics (e.g., prolonged stays), a fixed 1-week delay may misalign peak timing and distort amplitude.
proposals.rationale: Parsimonious alternative that encodes a short lag from infections to hospital admissions without introducing an explicit H compartment; suitable when H is weakly identifiable but lag is important.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true lag is shorter or changes over the season, a fixed 2-week delay can shift peaks too late and degrade short-horizon forecasts.
proposals.rationale: Captures a more realistic infection-to-admission lag for influenza in weekly data while keeping the model simple; can better align high peakiness with observed hospitalization timing.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Extra flexibility can overfit short series and create spurious secondary waves or overly persistent tails when the season is single-peaked.
proposals.rationale: Adds waning immunity to accommodate potential within-season susceptibility replenishment or multi-wave behavior while still using a lagged observation consistent with admissions timing.
